author: Russell Brand
description:
The UK government has announced it will ban access to social media for every child under the age of 16, framed entirely as an act of child protection. Russell Brand argues the real motive has nothing to do with children at all, pointing out that a society genuinely organized around protecting its young would look completely different, from the vaccines it offers to the food in school cafeterias to the strength of its communities. What the policy actually accomplishes, he says, is forcing every single person who uses the internet to tether their IP address to verifiable government ID, all under the cover of a cause no one would publicly oppose.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Before rehab, before Christianity, and long before any of the public scrutiny, Russell Brand was tripping on acid and smoking weed and having experiences he now believes were genuine encounters with another dimension of reality. He tells Tommy that drug addicts are deeply spiritual people, that the willingness to die for something by definition means you already sense there is something bigger than yourself, and that everything he experienced while high was pointing him toward the same truth he eventually found in Christ. He just did not have the language for it yet because he thought Christianity was about shutting people up and controlling them.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell Brand raises the question of whether the Church of England has any meaningful relationship left with Christianity or whether it has followed every other institution into the hands of the controlling interests that eventually capture them all. He draws a hard line: Christ is supreme king, above nation, above family, above everything, and his loyalty is absolute and non-negotiable. If forced to choose between loyalty to his own children and loyalty to Christ, there is no choice to be made. He closes with what he describes as his calling under the Great Commission, to tell people there is no answer except Jesus Christ.
